_disclosure: This is the buyer-advisor view of the technical team — editorial guidance, not a substitute for product IFU or local regulatory requirements.

dengue.position: For a distributor sourcing dengue rapid tests, stock the combined NS1 + IgM/IgG device rather than single-marker tests — it covers the full diagnostic window and cuts your rejection risk.
reasoning: NS1 catches the first week; IgM/IgG covers the later serology window — a combo widens coverage in one SKU.
Fewer SKUs to stock and document means lower inventory and registration burden.
Tropical markets want room-temperature-stable kits with CE — confirm both before you commit.

malaria.position: Buy the species-differentiating Pf/Pan test, not a Pf-only device — malaria treatment depends on species, and Pf-only misses P. vivax.
reasoning: Pf/Pan distinguishes falciparum from other species, which changes treatment.
HRP2-only tests can miss falciparum in HRP2-deletion regions — a Pan line adds a safety net.
Field programs value instrument-free, room-temperature-stable formats.

hiv-std.position: Treat every reactive HIV or syphilis rapid result as presumptive — your program is only as defensible as its confirmation pathway.
reasoning: Antibody tests have a window period and false-reactive risk; serial confirmation is non-negotiable.
Combined HIV/syphilis devices reduce steps in antenatal and blood-bank screening.
Document the national confirmation algorithm before you sell into a new market.

hepatitis.position: When sourcing hepatitis tests, separate screening from confirmation — anti-HCV is a screen, not a diagnosis, and your buyers must understand that.
reasoning: HBsAg detects active or chronic HBV; anti-HCV only indicates exposure — reflex to HCV RNA is required.
Blood-bank and antenatal programs run HBsAg/HCV/HIV/syphilis combos for throughput.
Selling a clear 'screen vs confirm' story protects you and your buyers from misuse.

hpylori.position: Prefer the stool antigen test over serology for H. pylori — it detects active infection and works for test-of-cure, which serology cannot.
reasoning: Antibody tests stay positive after treatment; stool antigen confirms eradication.
Test-and-treat decisions need active-infection detection, not exposure history.
PPI/antibiotic timing affects stool antigen — put that caveat on your datasheet.

respiratory.position: Sell the multiplex COVID/Flu/RSV combo, not single-target antigen tests — winter syndromic demand makes the combo the higher-margin, higher-utility SKU.
reasoning: Three viruses present identically; a combo resolves the differential in one test.
Antigen tests are fast but less sensitive — set buyer expectations and offer PCR confirmation.
Seasonal demand means inventory planning, not just product choice.

cardiac.position: Position cardiac rapid tests as triage tools, not lab replacements — the value is speed-to-triage, and overselling accuracy will backfire.
reasoning: Troponin is the reference marker; POC qualitative assays are for early triage, with serial lab confirmation.
D-dimer is for VTE exclusion — a negative result is the clinical value.
Hospitals buy panels (troponin + CK-MB + myoglobin + D-dimer) more than single markers.

doa-workplace.position: Lead with the multi-panel cup with adulteration checks — it is the highest-value DOA SKU for workplace programs, not the single-analyte strip.
reasoning: Panel cups with pH/specific-gravity/oxidant strips detect tampering at the point of collection.
SAMHSA-style cut-offs make your product defensible in regulated workplace programs.
Every positive is presumptive — sell the confirmatory workflow, not just the strip.

pregnancy-fertility.position: For pregnancy/fertility, compete on packaging and private label, not on the chemistry — hCG and LH are commodity tests, so retail differentiation is the moat.
reasoning: hCG/LH/FSH are high-volume, low-complexity — buyers choose on price, brand and packaging.
Private-label retail packaging is the margin lever.
fFN/iGFBP-1 are risk-stratification aids, not diagnostics — label them accordingly.

tumor.position: Sell tumor markers as monitoring aids, never as standalone cancer tests — the honest framing is the only sustainable one.
reasoning: PSA/AFP/CEA rise in benign conditions too; imaging and confirmatory testing are required.
Overclaiming a cancer-screening use creates regulatory and reputational risk.
High-risk surveillance and monitoring are the legitimate, defensible use cases.

tropical.position: In tropical serology, lead with the cross-reactivity caveat — buyers who understand flavivirus overlap are buyers who don't return product.
reasoning: Dengue/Zika/chikungunya serology cross-reacts; interpretation needs epidemiological context.
Field programs value room-temperature stability and instrument-free formats above all.
Bulk/tender supply with full documentation is where the margin is.

gastrointestinal.position: Bundle the gastro panel — rota/adeno/noro combo plus calprotectin — because primary-care buyers want one supplier for the whole GI screen.
reasoning: Viral gastro combos cover the common pediatric pathogens in one device.
Calprotectin/lactoferrin add the IBD-vs-functional distinction that GPs ask for.
Low-MOQ, mixed-format catalog fill is the value for smaller distributors.
